sections.h2: Where is Groton, CT and how is the town laid out?
sections.html:
Groton is a town in New London County, on the east bank of the Thames River in southeastern Connecticut. It covers 45.3 square miles, and about 14.2 of those are water, so a large share of the town sits on or near the shoreline.

Groton is not one neighborhood. The town includes the City of Groton along the river, plus a string of separate communities that buyers and agents treat as different markets. If you own a house here, it helps to know which one you are in, because taxes, fire coverage and sewer billing can differ from one to the next.

  • City of Groton and Groton Heights (also called Groton Bank), along the Thames
  • Poquonnock Bridge, Center Groton, Fort Hill and Long Hill
  • Noank, Mystic and Old Mystic, on the Mystic River side
  • Groton Long Point, Eastern Point and Mumford Cove on the Sound
  • The submarine base area, which the Census Bureau lists as Conning Towers-Nautilus Park

Mystic is split between Groton and the neighboring town of Stonington. A Mystic address does not tell you which town taxes the house, so check the town line before you look up a tax bill. The community list comes from the Groton article on Wikipedia.

sections.h2: What is Groton's history, and why does it matter for a house sale?
sections.html:
Groton separated from New London in 1705, and it was a shipbuilding and whaling town long before it became a submarine town. Housing here has always followed the waterfront industry.

The Naval Submarine Base New London was founded in Groton in 1872 as a navy yard, and submarines were first based there in 1915. Electric Boat built USS Cuttlefish in Groton in 1931, and in 1954 it launched USS Nautilus, the first nuclear-powered submarine. Groton had already lost its northern section in 1836, when Ledyard split off as its own town.

That long industrial record means a mix of housing ages. Older homes near the river and in Noank sit alongside postwar neighborhoods built when the population doubled between 1940 and 1950, according to the census figures on the same Wikipedia page. The 2020 census counted 38,411 residents.

For a seller, age matters in practical ways: older wiring and plumbing, oil heat, and aging roofs show up in inspection reports. A buyer who pays cash for a house as it stands takes those items on directly instead of asking you to fix them first.

sections.h2: Who are the biggest employers in Groton?
sections.html:
The three largest employers in Groton are the Naval Submarine Base New London, General Dynamics Electric Boat and Pfizer. The town's 2022 annual financial report, as summarized on Wikipedia, lists these top employers:

Electric Boat and the base shape the local housing cycle more than any other factor. Households tied to the base or the shipyard can face a transfer or a new job with a fixed date, and a house that has to sell on that timeline is a common situation here. Pfizer also keeps a research and development campus in town on 137 acres.

If your job is changing and your closing date is fixed, a sale with no repair list and no showings can fit better than a listing that may take months. Weigh that against what the open market could bring, and compare more than one option.

sections.h2: How does Groton's climate affect an older house?
sections.html:
Groton has a humid continental climate with cold winters and warm, damp summers. Climate normals for the New London and Groton station show about 48.9 inches of precipitation a year and 24.5 inches of snow.

January is the coldest month, with an average daily low near 24 degrees Fahrenheit. July highs average about 81 degrees. That range is hard on exterior wood, roofs and masonry, and the freeze and thaw cycles are where a lot of deferred maintenance shows up.

  • Roofs: check for lifted shingles and ice-dam staining under the eaves
  • Foundations: look for damp basements and old water staining
  • Heating systems: many older homes still run on oil, and a tired boiler is a frequent buyer objection
  • Windows and siding near the water: salt air speeds up wear

The town has not published a flood rule that we could confirm for this page, so for any house near the water, ask the Town of Groton about flood zone status before you list. A lender will ask the same question of a financed buyer, and a flood zone can slow a conventional closing.

sections.h2: What roads, transit and schools serve Groton?
sections.html:
Groton is served by local bus lines from Southeast Area Transit, and the town's public schools are run by Groton Public Schools. Wikipedia also notes that Groton-New London Airport, a state-owned field in the southeast of town, has had no scheduled passenger service since 2004.

Higher education is part of the local picture too. The Avery Point campus of the University of Connecticut sits in Groton, and the E.T. Grasso Southeastern Technical High School and the Marine Science Magnet High School serve students from the area.

Buyers tend to ask about school district and commute first. Confirm school assignment for any specific address with Groton Public Schools, since village names do not always match district lines.

sections.h2: How does property tax work for a Groton house?
sections.html:
The Town of Groton Tax Collector bills and collects the town's taxes and also collects for nine taxing districts and political subdivisions. That means two houses in Groton can carry different totals depending on which district they sit in.

The Tax Division is at 45 Fort Hill Road, Groton, CT 06340, and the phone is 860-441-6670, option 4. Questions about assessed value, exemptions and tax relief go to the Assessor at 860-441-6660, option 1. Questions about balances, payments and interest go to the Tax Collector. The office also bills 22 sewer benefit assessment systems, two water benefit assessment systems, and sewer use and landfill accounts, so a closing agent will want to check those balances along with the property tax line.

One detail from the town's own page is worth knowing. If you pay through your bank's online bill pay, the payment can reach the town several days later, and up to two weeks is common, so it can post as late even if your bank debited you on the due date. Payments through the town's website or Official Payments count from the time of your confirmation. The details are on the Town of Groton tax collection page.

We did not confirm the town's current due dates or revaluation year from an opened official page, so ask the Tax Collector for both before you plan a closing around them.

sections.h2: What does Connecticut's conveyance tax add to a Groton sale?
sections.html:
Connecticut charges a conveyance tax on most real estate deeds, and the town clerk collects it when the deed is recorded. Under Connecticut General Statutes section 12-494, the base rate is three-quarters of one percent to the state plus one-quarter of one percent to the town, on sales of $2,000 or more.

Higher rates apply in some cases. Residential property priced at $800,000 or more is taxed in tiers, and property used for anything other than residential purposes carries a higher state rate of 1.25 percent. The statute also lets targeted investment communities add up to another quarter of one percent. The full text of Chapter 223 is on the legislature's website.

The statute's index shows that payment of the tax and filing of the return are conditions of recording, so the tax is settled at closing. We did not confirm from an opened page whether Groton is a targeted investment community, so ask the Groton Town Clerk which rate applies before you estimate your net.

sections.h2: What choices do Groton sellers have?
sections.html:
A Groton seller can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house in its current condition. Each path trades time, cost and price differently.

  • Listing: usually the highest possible price, with repairs, showings and a closing that depends on the buyer's financing
  • Private sale: saves the agent fee, but you handle marketing, paperwork and negotiation
  • Cash sale: a faster, simpler closing with no repair list, and often a lower price than a fully prepared listing

Cash offers fit best when the house needs work, when a tenant or an estate complicates a listing, or when a move date is fixed. Get the offer in writing, read the closing statement, and compare it with what a listing would net after repairs and fees.

faqs.q: Is Groton, CT in New London County?
faqs.a: Yes. Groton is a town in New London County on the Thames River, in the Southeastern Connecticut Planning Region.

faqs.q: How many people live in Groton, CT?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 38,411 residents in the town. That figure covers the City of Groton and all the villages, including the submarine base area.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Groton property tax?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Collector at 860-441-6670, option 4, for bills and payments, and the Assessor at 860-441-6660, option 1, for assessed value and exemptions. The tax office is at 45 Fort Hill Road.

faqs.q: Does a Groton tax bill include fire district or sewer charges?
faqs.a: It can. The Tax Collector bills for nine taxing districts and also handles sewer use, sewer benefit assessments, water benefit assessments and landfill accounts, so ask for a full payoff before closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Groton house if it needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can list it as is, sell privately, or take a cash offer from a buyer who handles repairs after closing. A cash buyer will usually price the repairs into the offer.

faqs.q: What is the Connecticut conveyance tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: The base rate under section 12-494 is 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the town on the sale price. Higher rates apply to non-residential property and to residential sales of $800,000 or more.
Part of it. Mystic is a village split between the towns of Stonington and Groton, so the town line decides which tax office bills a given house.
